questions.q: Why isn't linking a baseline GPO to an OU proof that every setting in it actually applied to every machine?
options: GPOs always apply instantly and completely with no possible exceptions
Baseline GPOs cannot be overridden by any other GPO under any circumstances
A more specific GPO linked later can override one of its settings through normal GPO precedence, and other factors like WMI filters or slow-link detection can also cause a setting to not apply
Linking a GPO automatically guarantees every setting applies forever with no further checks needed
questions.explain: GPO precedence, WMI filters, slow-link processing, and OS-build compatibility can all cause a setting to silently not apply, even though the GPO is linked correctly.

questions.q: What does gpresult /h report.html /f actually show that simply confirming a GPO is linked in GPMC does not?
options: An RSoP report on a specific machine, showing exactly which GPO won each individual setting on that machine
The CPU and memory usage of the machine it's run on
A list of all user accounts in the domain, unrelated to Group Policy
A list of every GPO that has ever existed in the domain
questions.explain: gpresult produces a Resultant Set of Policy report that reveals which GPO actually won each setting on that one machine, exposing precedence conflicts a GPMC link list can't show.

questions.q: What is Microsoft Secure Score genuinely useful for, and what does it NOT prove?
options: It's useful for tracking hardening posture as a trend over time for leadership reporting, but it does not prove a specific control actually stops a specific attack technique on a specific machine
It has no legitimate use at all and should be ignored entirely
It only measures network bandwidth and has nothing to do with security controls
It proves with certainty that every control works against every real attack technique
questions.explain: Secure Score can rise for months while a forgotten, unprotected machine sits outside the baseline entirely — the score has no way to detect that kind of gap.

questions.q: What is the real difference between a tabletop exercise and a red team engagement?
options: A tabletop walks stakeholders through a scenario conceptually without touching a live system; a red team actually attempts the technique against real, hardened systems
A red team only tests network firewalls and never touches endpoint controls
They are two names for exactly the same activity with no practical difference
A tabletop exercise is more technically rigorous than a red team engagement
questions.explain: A tabletop is a conceptual walkthrough; a red team actively tests a control under real conditions, such as actually attempting a credential dump against a hardened host.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, what gap did the red team's credential-dumping test find that a rising Secure Score alone had not caught?
options: The red team found that Credential Guard does not work on any machine, ever
All twenty workstations were equally vulnerable regardless of any configuration
Two of twenty workstations were imaged before the baseline existed and never received the GPO, so Credential Guard never actually protected them
The red team discovered that Secure Score itself was reporting a negative number
questions.explain: 18 of 20 workstations were correctly protected, but 2 had never received the baseline GPO — a real gap only the active red-team test surfaced, not the trend metric.
